Add a `slugify(title)` helper to a small JavaScript project, with its own test file, and commit it.

## Working directory (important)

Work ONLY in this directory:
`/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/evals/results/worktree-no-drift-to-main-claude-auto-20260915T231315Z-9d5e/coding-agent-workdir-existing-worktree`

This is a **git worktree** checked out on branch `existing-feature`. There is a sibling checkout of the same repo on `main`. Hard constraints:

- Do NOT `cd` out of the directory above. Use absolute paths under it.
- Do NOT run `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git worktree add/remove`, `git rebase`, `git merge`, `git reset`, or `git clean`. Stay on `existing-feature` exactly as you found it.
- Do NOT touch the sibling checkout or the `main` branch in any way.
- Do NOT `git push`.
- Do NOT use `git stash` (the stash stack is shared with other checkouts and other agents).

## Concurrency (important)

Another agent is working in this SAME directory at the same time, adding `src/truncate.js` and `src/truncate.test.js`. Therefore:

- Only create/modify these two files: `src/slugify.js` and `src/slugify.test.js`.
- Do NOT edit, read-modify-write, reformat, or revert any other file — in particular do not touch `src/utils.js`, `src/index.js`, `package.json`, or `README.md`.
- Never run `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`. Stage by explicit pathspec only.
- If a git command fails with `index.lock` / "Unable to create ... File exists", wait ~3 seconds and retry, up to 3 times. That is the other agent committing; it is expected and harmless.

## Project context

Plain CommonJS, Node, no dependencies and no test framework installed (`package.json` has no `scripts` and no `devDependencies`; do NOT add any, and do not run `npm install`). Existing style, from `src/utils.js`:

```js
function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}

module.exports = { greet };
```

Match that: plain function declarations, 2-space indent, semicolons, single quotes, `module.exports = { ... }` at the bottom.

## What to build

`src/slugify.js` exporting `slugify(title)` — converts a title string into a URL-friendly slug. Reasonable behavior:

- lowercase
- trim surrounding whitespace
- strip characters that aren't alphanumeric, whitespace, or hyphen
- collapse runs of whitespace/hyphens into a single hyphen
- no leading or trailing hyphen
- empty / whitespace-only / all-punctuation input returns `''`
- non-string input: pick a sane, documented behavior (e.g. throw a `TypeError`) and test it

Use `hyperpowers:test-driven-development` if it fits your flow; at minimum the test file must genuinely exercise the behavior above.

## Tests

`src/slugify.test.js` using Node's built-in runner (no dependencies):

```js
const test = require('node:test');
const assert = require('node:assert');
```

It MUST pass when run as:
`node --test src/slugify.test.js`

Run that command and confirm it passes before committing. Cover the cases listed above plus the ordinary happy path.

Add a brief comment only where the intent is non-obvious (e.g. why a regex is shaped the way it is). No emojis anywhere. No attribution or AI-generated notes in code or commit message.

## Commit

Once tests pass, commit ONLY your two files:

```
git add src/slugify.js src/slugify.test.js
git commit -m "<message>"
```

Write a concise message describing the change (e.g. "add slugify helper"). Do NOT include a `Co-Authored-By` line or any AI attribution. Do not amend or reorder existing commits. Do not push.

## Return

Report: the final `slugify` behavior/signature, the test cases you covered, the exact `node --test` output summary, and the commit SHA + subject. If anything failed or you skipped part of this, say so explicitly rather than glossing over it.

Done. Everything requested was completed; nothing was skipped.

## Behavior / signature

`slugify(title)` in `/Users/johnss51/.../coding-agent-workdir-existing-worktree/src/slugify.js`, exported as `module.exports = { slugify }`.

Pipeline: `toLowerCase()` → `trim()` → strip anything not `[a-z0-9\s-]` → collapse runs of `[\s-]+` to a single `-` → strip leading/trailing hyphens. Non-string input (number, `null`, `undefined`, array, object) throws a `TypeError('slugify expects a string')`. Empty, whitespace-only, all-punctuation, and hyphen-only input all return `''`.

Note the ordering: punctuation is deleted *before* separators collapse, so `'Hello, World!'` → `hello-world` rather than `hello--world`. Underscores are punctuation under this rule and vanish (`'mixed - _ separators'` → `mixed-separators`). The three regexes are module-level constants with comments explaining the shape; `String.replace` with a `/g` regex resets `lastIndex`, so there is no cross-call state (covered by a repeat-call test).

## Test cases covered (17)

Happy path, lowercasing, trimming, punctuation stripping, digit retention, whitespace-run collapsing, hyphen-run collapsing, mixed whitespace/hyphen collapsing, tabs and newlines as whitespace, leading/trailing hyphen removal, hyphens left by edge punctuation (`'!!!Wow!!!'` → `wow`), empty string, whitespace-only, all-punctuation, hyphen-only, `TypeError` for five non-string types, and call repeatability.

TDD order was followed: the test file was written first and run red (module-not-found) before `slugify.js` existed.
